'''Rafe Roys Mazzeo''' (born 1961) is an American mathematician working in [[differential geometry]], [[microlocal analysis]], and [[partial differential equations]].<ref name="Stanford">{{Cite web|url=https://mathematics.stanford.edu/people/rafe-mazzeo|title=Rafe Mazzeo &#124; Mathematics|website=Mathematics.stanford.edu|access-date=7 November 2021}}</ref> He is currently a professor of mathematics. He served as the department chair at [[Stanford University]] from 2007 to 2010 and 2019–2022.<ref name="Stanford" />

==Education and career==
Mazzeo obtained his [[B.S.]] degree from [[MIT]] in 1982. He completed his [[Ph.D.]] in mathematics at MIT under the supervision of [[Richard Burt Melrose]] in 1986. His Ph.D. thesis was titled "Hodge cohomology of negatively curved manifolds."<ref name="personal"/> After obtaining his Ph.D. degree, Mazzeo joined Stanford University, where he became a full professor in 1997.<ref name="personal"/>

==Contributions==
Mazzeo has published more than 150 mathematics papers,<ref name="Research Gate">{{cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Rafe-Mazzeo|title=Rafe Mazzeo|website=Researchgate.net|access-date=7 November 2021}}</ref><ref name="scholar">{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=p3LpUV0AAAAJ&hl=en|title=Rafe Mazzeo|website=Scholar.google.com|access-date=7 November 2021}}</ref> and his work has been cited more than 5000 times.<ref name="scholar" /> His work has been published in many prestigious mathematics journals, including ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]'',<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mazzeo |first1=Rafe |author2=Yanir A. Rubinstein |author3=Thalia Jeffres |title=Kähler–Einstein metrics with edge singularities |journal=Annals of Mathematics |date=2016 |volume=183 |pages=95–176 |doi=10.4007/annals.2016.183.1.3 |url=https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2016/183-1/p03 |access-date=4 September 2021|arxiv=1105.5216 |s2cid=119306806 }}</ref> ''[[Inventiones Mathematicae]]'',<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mazzeo |first1=Rafe |author2=Frank Pacard |author3=Richard Schoen |author-link3=Richard Schoen |author4=Nick Korevaar |title=Refined asymptotics for constant scalar curvature metrics with isolated singularities |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |date=1999 |volume=135 |issue=2 |pages=233–272 |doi=10.1007/s002220050285 |arxiv=math/9807038 |bibcode=1999InMat.135..233K |s2cid=5536612 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s002220050285| access-date=5 September 2021}}</ref> and ''[[Duke Mathematical Journal]]''.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mazzeo |first1=Rafe |author2=Tamás Hausel |author3=Eugenie Hunsicker |title=Hodge cohomology of gravitational instantons |journal=Duke Mathematical Journal |date=2004 |volume=122 |issue=3 |pages=485–548 |doi=10.1215/S0012-7094-04-12233-X |s2cid=14883967 |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/duke-mathematical-journal/volume-122/issue-3/Hodge-cohomology-of-gravitational-instantons/10.1215/S0012-7094-04-12233-X.short |access-date=5 September 2021|arxiv=math/0207169 }}</ref> He has had 11 doctoral students.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=57664|title=Rafe Mazzeo - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=Genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=7 November 2021}}</ref> He is one of the founders of the [[Stanford University Mathematics Camp]]. He is Faculty Director of the Stanford Online High School, and has been Director of the IAS/Park City Mathematics Institute since 2015.

==Awards and fellowships==
Mazzeo has received many awards, including a [[National Science Foundation]] Postdoctoral Fellowship, [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] Research Fellowship, National Science Foundation Young Investigator Fellowship, and Louis and Claude Rosenberg Jr. University Fellowship in Undergraduate Education.<ref name="personal"/>

In 2013, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi|title=Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|website=American Mathematical Society|access-date=7 November 2021}}</ref> He was elected as a Member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/new-members-2022https://www.amacad.org/new-members-2022|title=New Members American Academy of Arts and Sciences|website=amacad.org|access-date=1 May 2022}}</ref>
